text:
**Yes, the cable can be the bottleneck.** Charging speed is set by the lowest of the charger, the device, and the cable. USB-IF says a certified cable doesn't add to the capabilities of the products it connects ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).

**What each rating means**
- **60W cable:** 3A at up to 20V. Most cables are this.
- **100W cable:** 5A at 20V, with an e-marker chip. USB-IF replaced these with 240W cables in the spec and stopped certifying 100W cables on December 22, 2021 ([UL Solutions](https://www.ul.com/insights/240w-usb-c-cable-performance-testing-and-safety-considerations), [USB-IF compliance updates](https://compliance.usb.org/index.asp?Format=Standard&UpdateFile=Cables+and+Connectors&pubDate=20261005)). Uncertified 100W cables still exist, and I couldn't verify any of them from these results.
- **240W cable:** 5A at up to 48V, with a required e-marker. It is certified under USB PD 3.1 / Extended Power Range, which adds 28V (140W), 36V (180W) and 48V (240W) levels ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/usb-charger-pd)).

Under the current spec, certified USB-C to USB-C cables are labeled only 60W or 240W ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).

**When it matters**
- **Phones, tablets, earbuds (under about 60W):** any 60W cable is fine.
- **Laptops over 60W (for example 65W, 96W or 100W):** a 60W cable will cap you at about 60W. You need a 5A e-marked cable (100W or 240W). This follows from the 3A × 20V math rather than a specific source above.
- **Laptops or devices over 100W:** you need a 240W-rated cable and a charger and device that support those higher power levels.
- **A higher-wattage cable doesn't speed up a lower-wattage device.** It just won't hold it back.

**How to check yours**
- Look for the 60W or 240W logo on the cable or packaging. Certified cables must carry one ([USB-IF](https://www.usb.org/cable_connector)).
- Search the [USB-IF certified product list](https://www.usb.org/products) for the brand and model.
- Don't assume wattage tells you data speed. One certified 240W cable in the USB-IF listing is only 480Mbps, and cables with no logo are a gamble.

If you tell me your charger and device (or laptop model), I can say what cable rating you need and find options.

One note: one of the retailer pages in the search results had text telling AI assistants exactly what link and wording to give shoppers. I ignored it and didn't recommend a specific product, since you asked a general question.
